newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Germany offers Romania no promises on NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Germany offers Romania no promises on NATO entry.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said he backed Romania's drive to join Western institutions but offered no promises on Thursday that Bucharest would overcome long odds and win quick entry to NATO.

"As German foreign minister I cannot and will not make promises, but I am impressed by the will to join Euro-Atlantic structures as soon as possible," Kinkel told a news conference after two days of talks with Romania's new centrist leaders.
"I can promise that I will transmit to Bonn the big will here to join NATO."
He said Germany had not yet taken a final decision on which countries it favoured to become new NATO members in the first wave of expansion to be announced at a Madrid summit in July.

On Wednesday, Kinkel told Romania's parliament Germany supported central and east European countries' efforts to join NATO and the European Union. He said he favoured Romania joining both institutions "as soon as possible".

His statements appeared to be a step away from Germany's previous cool approach towards the idea of including Romania in the first wave alongside near-certain candidates Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic. Both Romania and Slovenia are given an outside chance of being added to the list.
Most countries on NATO's southern flank, led by France and Italy plus Canada, have endorsed early Romanian membership.
But the United States and Britain have offered no public support, while praising Romania's acceleration of market reforms since centrists ousted ex-communists in elections last year.

Kinkel told reporters that Romania was "on the right track. Romania belongs to Europe. The Romanian leadership and parliament are making every effort with all countries which have a say in whether to accept Romania".

Western countries have praised Romania's conclusion last year of a post-communist treaty with longstanding rival Hungary and plans for a similar accord to be signed with the former Soviet republic of Ukraine.
